question: Which Bengali newspaper was founded and edited by Raja Rammohan Roy?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sambad kaunmudi**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Rammohan Roy** was one of the **founders of the Brahmo Sabha**, the precursor of the Brahmo Samaj, which was a social-religious reform movement in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• He **had started two newspapers- one in Bangali, which was known as the Sambad kumudi, and another in Persian, which was called the Mirat-ul-Akbar.**
 
• Given below refers to a brief description of the two newspapers:
 
 
• Sambad Kumudi:
 
 
• It referred to a Bengali weekly newspaper that was published in Kolkata during the first half of the 19th century by Ram Mohan Roy.
 
• It mentioned a noted pro-reformist publication that had actively campaigned for the abolition (stop) of the Sati Pratha.
 
 
 
• Mirat-ul-Akhbar (Mirror of News):
 
 
• It referred to a Persian language journal rant that was founded as well as edited by Raja Rammohan Roy
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marathi**

 
 
• It is the newspaper that was started by Bal Gangadhar Tilak in 1881.
 
 
 
• **Kesari**
 
 
• It was **written by Lokmanya Tilak** during the Indian National Movement
 
• The newspaper was initially founded in 1881 
 
• The Kesari newspaper was originally started as a co-operative effort by Agarkar (the paper’s first editor), Chiplunkar, and Tilak, and was published along with Tilak’s English newspaper, the Mahratta, to encourage people to rise against the oppressive regime of the time, instead of being submissive.
